chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Jeong Fire is the candle, and when you connect, you connect deeply. Even an undefined thing feels intimate to you, because you bring your whole attention to it. You stay because the moments feel so real: the late talks, the small details they remember, the rare feeling of being understood. The question is whether that intimacy runs in both directions, or whether you're doing most of the feeling and quietly calling it us. Your depth is a gift. Make sure it's being received, not just enjoyed from a comfortable distance.
text.what-you-want: Being special to them is what you want, in a clear and steady way. Jeong Fire doesn't do half-attachments well, and you probably already feel more than you've admitted to anyone, including yourself. Write it down honestly: what would make you feel safe here? Consistent contact, knowing you're the only one, a simple name for what this is? Owning that want isn't needy. It's accurate. A candle needs a still room to burn well, and wanting stillness is not too much to ask of someone you're close to. Say it to yourself first, in a full sentence, so it sounds familiar when you say it to them.
text.mixed-signals: Mixed signals are your weak spot. Jeong Fire reads every detail and builds meaning from it. A late reply becomes a whole story, a heart emoji becomes a different one, a full stop becomes a tragedy. Your intuition is often right, but in uncertainty it works overtime and runs out of facts. Try one rule: one interpretation per day, maximum. Then go and do something else with your hands. And notice this: if a person's messages need this much decoding, the message itself is unclear, and that is information too.
text.the-talk: When you have the talk, it should be calm and in person if you can manage it, at a time when you're rested rather than wound up. Jeong Fire has more courage than people realize, and you're good with honest, intimate words. Say what you feel, briefly: I've gotten attached, and I'd like to know where you are. Then let them answer without filling the silence with reassurance or a quick it's okay if not. You don't need to protect them from your feelings. They're allowed to hold them for a moment. Breathe, keep your hands busy with a cup of tea, and trust that your voice will hold steady enough.
text.your-line: Your dealbreaker is about consistency. Jeong Fire can't relax in hot and cold. Decide in advance what counts as too much uncertainty for you: days without contact, plans that keep vanishing, feeling anxious more often than happy. When you hit that line, you step back to protect your flame. That isn't punishment, and it isn't a test to see if they chase you. It's maintenance. A candle in a drafty room either gets moved or goes out, and you get to choose the first option. Write the line down on a calm day, so the anxious version of you at midnight can't quietly rewrite it.
text.either-way: Whatever they say, you'll feel it deeply, and you'll be okay. If they want more, beautiful, build it slowly and keep talking honestly as you go. If not, the candle doesn't go out just because one person walked past it. Give yourself quiet, gentle days, time with people who already love you, and some patience. Your capacity for closeness is still fully there, waiting for someone who wants all of it, the depth, the attention, the moods, and treats that as the best part. Light something warm, call someone who knows you well, and let that be enough for one evening.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You bring so much depth to this, Jeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And they bring... a heart emoji every four days.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Wanting to feel special isn't needy.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One interpretation per day. You're on number nine.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say how you feel. Calmly. You're braver than you think.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: If it needs this much decoding, that's the message.

spring.intro: A candle in spring has kindling everywhere. Wood ruled your birth season and feeds your Fire, so you have plenty of emotional fuel and you spend it on one person. In a situationship you probably think about them more than you'd admit, rereading messages, noticing every shift in tone. Every small spark feels like evidence. The spring blind spot is that a candle can burn brightly on its own fuel, which means you can feel a whole romance while they feel a nice thing. Check the kindling. How much of this fire is coming from them? You deserve someone who adds wood, not someone who only warms their hands.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've read meaning into a single heart emoji for three days. It's an emoji.

summer.intro: Summer Jeong burns with focused heat. Fire ruled your birth season and doubled your element, which makes you loyal, intense and selective about who gets close. Once you've chosen someone, a situationship doesn't feel casual to you at all. It feels like devotion without a title. You might be acting more committed than they are, then feeling quietly furious about it. Summer Jeong's habit is to keep burning and say nothing until the flame flares into a fight. Say it before then, calmly. Tell them you're exclusive in your head and ask where they are. Your intensity deserves clarity, not a slow burn on hope.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're already all in. It's fair to ask if they are too.

autumn.intro: Autumn Jeong is the careful flame that works on metal. Metal ruled your season, and Fire shapes Metal, so you love by attending to details and making things just right. In a situationship you've likely been quietly shaping it: the right timing, the right tone, the perfect moment to bring it up that never quite arrives. You're waiting for ideal conditions. They won't come. Autumn Jeong's trap is perfectionism disguised as patience. The talk doesn't need to be beautiful. It needs to happen. A plain question asked kindly will tell you more than a month of carefully crafted hints.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The perfect moment for the talk does not exist. Pick a Tuesday.

winter.intro: A winter candle guards itself against every draft. Your birth season belonged to Water, Jeong, and Water puts out Fire, so you learned to protect your feelings carefully. In a situationship that can mean you keep things undefined on purpose. If nothing is official, nothing can be lost. You give warmth in small, safe doses and tell yourself you don't mind the vagueness. Part of you does. Winter Jeong's honest question is whether this arrangement is protecting your flame or starving it. A candle in a sealed jar goes out too. Let a little air in. Ask for something you want.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Keeping it undefined feels safer. Is it actually keeping you warm, Jeong?

earth.intro: The last weeks of a season are the Earth days, and you were born in them, Jeong. A candle in a clay room: your warmth stays close and makes the space feel safe. Fire feeds Earth, so in a situationship you create comfort, and comfort is easy to stay in without naming. You read every small signal, then keep your conclusions to yourself. The drift is two people getting cozy without deciding anything. The talk for you can be gentle and specific: one sentence about what you feel, one question about what they want.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Cozy isn't the same as clear, Jeong. You're allowed to want both.

strength.strong: Your candle has plenty of fuel, Jeong, so your focus gets intense once someone matters. In a situationship you might be pushing for clarity in ways that feel like pressure to them: frequent check-ins, detailed questions, reading into every word. Your care is real. The blind spot is that a steady flame held too close starts to feel like heat. Give the question one clear moment instead of fifty small ones. Ask what they want, say what you want, then let the answer arrive at its own pace without chasing it.
strength.weak: With little support for your Day Master, Jeong, you guard your flame carefully at first, then give far too much of it once you're in. In a situationship you might be pouring attention into someone who offers a flicker back. You remember everything about them. Do they remember your stuff? The blind spot is accepting thin warmth because losing even that feels unbearable. You deserve someone who tends your flame too. Notice who asks how your day went without being prompted. Start there.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practice clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyze every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analyzed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: The timetable and the 1 a.m. paragraph
gap-wood.text: You probably fell for the Gap Wood because they're solid. They say what they mean, they turn up on time, they hold the umbrella over you without making a thing of it. And yet their texts read like logistics. You send something soft and late at night, the kind of message you rewrote twice, and the answer is 'haha yes, Saturday works'. You notice the shortness. You always notice. Here is the thing about a Gap: silence means fine to them. If you go quiet because something hurt, Gap often just assumes you're busy. Testing them, by waiting to see if they ask or by liking their story and not replying, tends to go straight past a tree. The drift happens in the space between your hints and their literal reading of the world. The talk is where you get to stop hinting. Gap respects directness, so say it plainly: I like you a lot, and I don't want to keep guessing what this is. Can we name it? Say it in daylight, not at 1 a.m. Gap Wood is usually far more comfortable with a clear question than with a riddle, and you deserve a clear answer.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, your 1 a.m. paragraphs are lovely. Gap reads them like weather reports.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap doesn't do subtext. Hinting at a tree is a hobby, not a plan.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap needs to send one detail back. That's all the candle needs.

eul-wood.title: Love letters disguised as texts
eul-wood.text: An Eul Wood is soft, romantic and wonderful at making you feel noticed, until you see them making everyone else feel noticed too. Eul has a big social garden. You have one candle and you'd like to keep it lit in one room. That difference is where this situationship gets tender. The drift isn't loud. Neither of you likes conflict, so when something stings, Eul goes vague and you go quiet. You might start counting how many stories Eul posted from parties you weren't at, or asking casual questions about who was there that aren't really casual. Eul tends to hear those questions as pressure and slip a little further out of reach, and the loop tightens. Your messages to each other are long and lovely, and they're also where the real topic gets avoided. You're both fluent in subtext, so nobody says the plain thing. For the talk, say what you need without asking Eul to shrink their world: I love how social you are. I'd also like to know I'm your person, not one of many. Can we make this official? Then trust the answer instead of auditing it. Your flame burns best when it isn't guarding the door.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You two write love letters disguised as texts. Gorgeous.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And neither of you has said the actual thing. Code word, please.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, ask for focus. Eul, give it out loud.

byeong-fire.title: Message number thirty-nine
byeong-fire.text: Byeong Fire is the sun, and for a while you get to stand in it. The energy is incredible: calls on the way home, spontaneous plans, the kind of laugh that makes you laugh too. Then you check your phone and see Byeong replied to the group chat, liked six stories and sent a meme to their cousin, and your message is still sitting there. That's the drift. Byeong gives warmth to everyone, and you'd like it focused. When it isn't, you start to feel like one of Byeong's many friends instead of the one, and you might go quiet and wait to be noticed. Suns don't always notice quiet. Byeong's texts are short, loud and frequent, and in a situationship that can look like casualness. Yours are fewer and deeper, and Byeong might find them heavy without meaning to. When it flares, it flares fast, and you hold the details for longer. For the talk, assume good intent and still ask clearly: I like you a lot, and I want to be your person, not part of the crowd. Would that work for you? Say it before you start keeping score. Byeong tends to answer warmth with warmth.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Same element, different rooms. The sun and the candle.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong replying to Jeong first is not hard. It's a choice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, assume warmth. Then ask clearly.

jeong-fire.title: The candlelit staring contest
jeong-fire.text: Two Jeong Fires in a situationship create the most intimate candlelit room in the building. You understand each other's moods without explanation. Your messages are long, careful and emotionally precise, and you both notice when the other switches from 'haha' to 'ha'. That precision is beautiful, and it's also the trap. The drift here is waiting. Both of you process feelings internally and expect, quietly, to be read. So when something's off, you each wait for the other to notice, and the room goes dark. The 'what are we' question becomes a staring contest: who will admit they want it first? Jealousy can also run hot, because you both love in a focused way. A like on someone else's photo can turn into a three-day silence that nobody explains. And you both keep a detailed archive of every slightly short reply. For the talk, someone has to stop being read and start speaking. Do it in daylight, when neither of you is tired: I want us to be exclusive. I've wanted it for a while. Do you? And make a deal while you're there: a short reply is a busy day, not a verdict.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two candles. Nobody understands you like each other.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And nobody waits longer to say it. Staring contest over.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A short reply is a busy day. Not a verdict.

mu-earth.title: 'Yes, it was good' and the lantern rereading it
mu-earth.text: A Mu Earth is the mountain temple your lantern has been looking for. Steady, quiet, safe. Mu always replies, even if it's three words and four hours later. Mu turns up when they say they will. Mu fixes your shelf without being asked. You feel held. The drift is that Mu doesn't say much about feelings, and you need feelings said. You send a long, heartfelt message about the evening you spent together, and Mu replies 'yes, it was good'. You read it four times looking for more. There isn't more, and also, for Mu, there was a lot in that sentence. When you're anxious about what this is, Mu tends to say 'it's fine' and mean it completely, which is somehow not reassuring. If you go quiet because you're hurt, Mu may not notice until it's a fire. Your signal is depth, and Mu may simply not see it unless it's spoken. For the talk, use the simplest repair there is. Say it in one sentence: I want us to be official. Then ask Mu to say back what they heard. Feeling heard does most of the work here. Read Mu's reliability as the love it is.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A lantern in the mountain temple. Warm, quiet, lasting.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu's 'it's fine' is not a reply to a paragraph.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: One sentence, repeated back. That's the whole repair.

gi-earth.title: 'Are we okay?' answered with 'did you eat?'
gi-earth.text: With a Gi Earth, you get candlelight in the kitchen: cozy, caring and very domestic in the best way. Gi makes sure you ate. Gi texts 'home safe?' after every date. Gi knows you hate coriander and quietly removes it from your half. It feels like being looked after, which you love. The drift here is two worriers in one room. You worry about feelings: are we okay, did I say too much, is this going anywhere. Gi worries about practical things: did you sleep, is your rent sorted, should we book the train. When you ask 'are we okay?', Gi might answer with 'did you eat?', and you both feel slightly unheard. Neither of you likes direct conflict, so the 'what are we' question can go round and round in two separate heads. You may start to feel Gi is too focused on tasks. Gi may feel you're too focused on emotions. Your signal is the feelings question, which Gi may read as stress to fix. For the talk, answer Gi's practical question first, then ask yours in plain words: Yes, I've eaten. And I'd like us to be together properly. Are you up for that?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Candlelight in the kitchen. So cozy it hurts.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'Are we okay?' is not answered by 'did you eat?'

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Answer their question first. Then ask yours.

gyeong-metal.title: Forgotten by dinner, replayed at midnight
gyeong-metal.text: A Gyeong Metal is raw steel, and you're the patient heat that could shape it. You admire their directness, their competence, the way they protect people without making speeches about it. And sometimes they say something blunt that you're still replaying at midnight, while Gyeong forgot it by dinner. That memory gap is the drift in this situationship. You hold onto the small cuts. Gyeong moves on and assumes all is well. When you're hurt, you communicate in code: a shorter text, a cooler emoji, a story post that means something. Gyeong doesn't read code. Gyeong wants things said plainly, and gets frustrated by what feels like riddles. You might also be quietly trying to soften Gyeong's edges, and Gyeong can feel that as being 'improved'. The 'what are we' question tends to sit in your chest while Gyeong assumes it's obvious. Your signal is subtle, and steel misses subtle. For the talk, say the actual thing. Plainly, without testing first: I'd like us to be a couple. I need to hear whether you want that. Gyeong respects a straight question. And when something stings, say so the same day, before it turns into a midnight replay.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Patient heat, slow shaping. This can be something.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong forgot the fight by dinner. Jeong is still drafting a reply.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say it the same day. No midnight replays.

sin-metal.title: The comment at dinner with friends
sin-metal.text: A Sin Metal is the beautiful silver your flame wants to be near. They're refined, sharp and quietly funny, and you feel very seen when they notice something about you no one else does. You also feel very seen when they notice something you'd rather they hadn't. The drift in this situationship is two sensitive people circling each other. Your intensity can feel like pressure to Sin, who likes poise and space. Sin's precise little critiques can sting you more than Sin realizes. When either of you is hurt, you both withdraw, and the tension simmers in carefully crafted, overanalyzed texts. You might start to read Sin's distance as coldness. Sin might start to read your closeness as possessive. The flash point tends to be public: a comment at dinner with friends that you take as a review of you. Your signal is focus, which can feel heavy to someone who needs air. For the talk, choose a private place and lower the stakes first. A silly selfie the day before helps. Then: I like you a lot. I'd like us to be exclusive. Would you? Keep it short. Long can feel like pressure here.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A flame near silver. Beautiful and very, very careful.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Feedback at dinner with friends? Save it for the walk home.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Send the silly selfie. Then have the talk.

im-water.title: A lantern on the river at midnight
im-water.text: 丁 and 壬 form a heavenly combination: a lantern reflected on the river. With an Im Water, you feel it. The conversations are deep and strangely easy. Im sends you a three-paragraph thought at midnight about why people collect things, and you reply with something that makes them say 'exactly'. You feel understood at a level that's almost unsettling. The drift comes from how differently you hold closeness. You want it steady and focused. Im needs freedom, and goes quiet to think, travel, or follow a new idea for a while. That quiet makes you anxious. You might reach for reassurance, check if they've been online, ask a pointed question about the weekend. Im can feel the walls closing and drift a little further, and the cycle repeats. Nobody names it, so it feels like fate rather than a pattern. Your signal is devotion, which can feel like a fence to a river. For the talk, trust the rhythm first. Then be clear: I don't need you around all the time. I do need to know we're together. Can we say that out loud? Ask Im for one small check-in when they disappear into their head. It's a fair request.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 丁壬, a lantern on the river. Deep, easy, rare.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im vanishes into their head without a word. One line would do.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, trust the rhythm, and still ask for what you need.

gye-water.title: Waiting in the rain for a knock
gye-water.text: A Gye Water is tender, sad-eyed and deeply sensitive, which is exactly what draws you in. You both feel things a lot. You send each other songs and long messages at 1 a.m. that feel like reading someone's diary. And then a silence, sometimes two days long, that nobody explains. The drift in this situationship lives in those silences. Gye's moods come and go like rain, and when Gye withdraws, your flame flickers into anxiety. You want clarity: are we okay, what is this, where did you go. Gye can feel those questions as invasive and go further into the mist. Then you're hurt, and you withdraw too, and the situationship becomes two people waiting in the rain for the other to knock. Gye's mystery can trigger your worst worries, and your need to know can feel like pressure to Gye. Your signal is intensity, which can feel like too much heat for someone this quiet. For the talk, lower the pressure and set a gentle rule: I like you so much. I'd love for us to be together. And can we agree that silence is allowed, but never as punishment? Then let Gye take time to answer.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two very soft hearts. Gentle with each other, please.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Silence is allowed. Silence as punishment is not.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, one clear sentence. Jeong, one deep breath.
